## Summary

Adds a fused W4A16 Triton kernel (`awq_gemm_fused_fp32`) that unpacks AWQ int4 weights and performs the GEMM without materializing the full FP16 weight, replacing the existing full-dequantize + `torch.matmul` path under `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1` for AWQ Triton (`AutoAWQLinearMethod`). Scoped to SM89, FP16 activations/scales, asymmetric AWQ int4, group size 128, contiguous tensors, K a multiple of the group size, N aligned to 32; all other configurations keep the existing fallback unchanged.

## Why this is not a duplicate

- Searched #27433 (the batch-invariance tracking issue) and its comments — no existing claim or in-progress work on an AWQ-specific fused kernel.
- `gh pr list --search "awq_gemm_fused"` / `"auto_awq.py in:body"` / `"awq_triton in:body"` and `gh search code --owner vllm-project "awq_gemm_fused_fp32"` all return no hits.
- #46639 (Marlin MoE batch invariance) and #53403 (docs: tested-models list) touch related but disjoint code (Marlin MoE, not AWQ Triton GEMM).

## Test commands and results

```
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/kernels/quantization/test_awq_triton.py -v
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/quantization/test_auto_awq.py -v
```
65/65 pass on a real RTX 4090 (SM89): 48 shape-sweep cases (incl. tiling-boundary M=127/128/129), 5 validation-rejection cases, 8 batch-invariance byte-exact cases (`torch.equal` on raw bytes, not `assert_close`, so +0.0/-0.0 can't hide), 4 dispatch cases (contiguity-independence, BI-off, unsupported group-size, real-model integration).

**Independent numerical check**: a from-scratch NumPy FP64 reference (no vLLM dequant code reused) against the real `Qwen/Qwen3-4B-AWQ` checkpoint weights, 4 real projection shapes (qkv/o/gate_up/down) at M=1/32/129. Fused kernel's max abs error vs. this reference is consistently at or below the existing dequant+matmul path's error vs. the same reference, at every shape and M tested (including M=129, a large-M point not covered by the byte-exact batch-invariance tests).

**Real-engine checks** (`vllm.LLM`, Qwen3-4B-AWQ, real Attention + paged KV cache):
- BS1 vs BS32 and prefill-vs-decode logprobs: bit-exact (max abs diff 0.0).
- CUDA graph capture/replay: eager vs. compiled match at M=128/129/256, contiguous and non-contiguous inputs, including replay after buffer update.
- Baseline (legacy dequant+matmul) vs. fused kernel next-token logprobs on 3 fixed prefixes (24/85/391 chars): top-1 token matches on all 3; max logprob diff ~1.3e-2 to 2.3e-2. This is a numerical spot-check, not a bit-exactness claim — the two algorithms use different reduction orders and are not expected to be identical, only both individually batch-invariant.

## Model evaluation

Full GSM8K (1319 questions, 5-shot, greedy), same checkpoint/prompts/decoding config, baseline (`VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=0`) vs. prototype (`VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1`, exercising the fused kernel):
- Baseline accuracy: 82.87%. Prototype: 82.94%. Δ +0.08pp (~1 question of 1319). Invalid rate 0.0% both arms.

## Performance

ABBA methodology (order A→C1→C1→A, isolated caches, no profiler, SHA-256 hash of output tokens to confirm determinism) on 5 workloads (decode B1/B8/B32, long-context B1, mixed B8), RTX 4090:

| Workload | Wall reduction | Throughput gain | Peak mem reduction |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| decode_b1 | +54.6% | +120.3% | 157.1 MiB |
| decode_b8 | +55.6% | +125.3% | 144.0 MiB |
| decode_b32 | +51.3% | +105.5% | 111.5 MiB |
| long_b1 | +31.2% | +45.3% | 111.5 MiB |
| mixed_b8 | +34.7% | +53.1% | 110.8 MiB |

All output-token hashes matched across all 4 processes/both arms for every workload (confirms determinism, not just aggregate timing).

## Known limitations

- The fused kernel is not yet in vLLM's JIT kernel-warmup path, so the first live inference call compiles it inline (observed latency spike). Warmup registration is out of scope for this PR.
- An unrelated, pre-existing lm_head `OutOfResources` (shared memory) bug in vLLM's own `linear_batch_invariant` persistent-matmul kernel was reproduced via one lightweight test harness at this vocab size; not related to this patch, not yet filed upstream, root cause not confirmed.

## AI assistance disclosure

This PR was developed with Claude Code (Anthropic) assistance: kernel implementation, bug review, test authoring, and verification script development. All changed lines were reviewed by the human submitter (@ShengleiFu), who ran the test commands above and is able to defend this change end-to-end.

Thank you @yewentao256  for the feedback! Addressed both:

## 1. Diff size

Shrunk from ~566 to ~420 lines, kept only the regression tests tied to a specific bug fixed in this PR (group-count OOB validation, contiguity-independent dispatch) plus core shape-correctness and batch-invariance coverage. 

## 2. `lm_eval` — end-to-end accuracy

GSM8K, 5-shot, n=1319, same checkpoint (`Qwen/Qwen3-4B-AWQ`) and decoding config for both arms:

| Arm | strict-match | flexible-extract |
|---|---:|---:|
| Baseline (`VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=0`) | 83.78% ± 1.02 | 81.43% ± 1.07 |
| This PR (`VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1`, fused kernel) | 83.62% ± 1.02 | 81.20% ± 1.08 |

Both deltas are within stderr — no accuracy regression.

```
lm-eval run --model vllm \
  --model_args pretrained=Qwen/Qwen3-4B-AWQ,dtype=float16,quantization=auto_awq,max_model_len=2048,gpu_memory_utilization=0.85,trust_remote_code=True \
  --tasks gsm8k --batch_size auto
```

## 3. `vllm bench serve` — end-to-end perf

Both arms run with `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1` (the fused kernel only activates under batch-invariant mode, so a `BI=0` vs `BI=1` comparison would conflate "cost of batch-invariant mode itself" with "this kernel's effect," which isn't what this PR claims). Isolated legacy-dequant+matmul vs. the fused kernel via a `sitecustomize.py` monkeypatch of `awq_gemm_fused_fp32`, loaded into both the API server and its spawned engine-core worker via `PYTHONPATH` — real multiprocess `vllm serve`, not an in-process shortcut.

```
vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-4B-AWQ --quantization auto_awq --dtype float16 --max-model-len 2048 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.85 --trust-remote-code

vllm bench serve --backend vllm --model Qwen/Qwen3-4B-AWQ --dataset-name random \
  --random-input-len 512 --random-output-len 128 --num-prompts 200 --seed 0
```

Steady-state (2nd/3rd pass against an already-running server; see "Known limitations" for why the first pass is excluded):

| Arm | Mean TPOT | Output tok/s |
|---|---:|---:|
| Legacy (dequant+matmul) | ~59.7ms | ~3118 |
| This PR (fused kernel) | ~49.3ms | ~3180 |

~17% lower per-token decode latency, comparable-or-slightly-higher throughput.

**Known limitation surfaced by this run**: the fused kernel isn't yet in vLLM's JIT kernel-warmup path, so the very first live request against a freshly started server compiles it inline (one-time latency spike, logged as `Triton kernel JIT compilation during inference: awq_gemm_fused_fp32_kernel`). The table above reflects steady-state after that one-time cost; a production deployment would want warmup registration added (tracked as follow-up, not blocking this PR's correctness/perf claim).

detail.body:
## Summary

Adds a fused W4A16 Triton kernel (`awq_gemm_fused_fp32`) that unpacks AWQ int4 weights and performs the GEMM without materializing the full FP16 weight, replacing the existing full-dequantize + `torch.matmul` path under `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1` for AWQ Triton (`AutoAWQLinearMethod`). Scoped to SM89, FP16 activations/scales, asymmetric AWQ int4, group size 128, contiguous tensors, K a multiple of the group size, N aligned to 32; all other configurations keep the existing fallback unchanged.

## Why this is not a duplicate

- Searched #27433 (the batch-invariance tracking issue) and its comments — no existing claim or in-progress work on an AWQ-specific fused kernel.
- `gh pr list --search "awq_gemm_fused"` / `"auto_awq.py in:body"` / `"awq_triton in:body"` and `gh search code --owner vllm-project "awq_gemm_fused_fp32"` all return no hits.
- #46639 (Marlin MoE batch invariance) and #53403 (docs: tested-models list) touch related but disjoint code (Marlin MoE, not AWQ Triton GEMM).

## Test commands and results

```
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/kernels/quantization/test_awq_triton.py -v
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/quantization/test_auto_awq.py -v
```
65/65 pass on a real RTX 4090 (SM89): 48 shape-sweep cases (incl. tiling-boundary M=127/128/129), 5 validation-rejection cases, 8 batch-invariance byte-exact cases (`torch.equal` on raw bytes, not `assert_close`, so +0.0/-0.0 can't hide), 4 dispatch cases (contiguity-independence, BI-off, unsupported group-size, real-model integration).

**Independent numerical check**: a from-scratch NumPy FP64 reference (no vLLM dequant code reused) against the real `Qwen/Qwen3-4B-AWQ` checkpoint weights, 4 real projection shapes (qkv/o/gate_up/down) at M=1/32/129. Fused kernel's max abs error vs. this reference is consistently at or below the existing dequant+matmul path's error vs. the same reference, at every shape and M tested (including M=129, a large-M point not covered by the byte-exact batch-invariance tests).

**Real-engine checks** (`vllm.LLM`, Qwen3-4B-AWQ, real Attention + paged KV cache):
- BS1 vs BS32 and prefill-vs-decode logprobs: bit-exact (max abs diff 0.0).
- CUDA graph capture/replay: eager vs. compiled match at M=128/129/256, contiguous and non-contiguous inputs, including replay after buffer update.
- Baseline (legacy dequant+matmul) vs. fused kernel next-token logprobs on 3 fixed prefixes (24/85/391 chars): top-1 token matches on all 3; max logprob diff ~1.3e-2 to 2.3e-2. This is a numerical spot-check, not a bit-exactness claim — the two algorithms use different reduction orders and are not expected to be identical, only both individually batch-invariant.

## Model evaluation

Full GSM8K (1319 questions, 5-shot, greedy), same checkpoint/prompts/decoding config, baseline (`VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=0`) vs. prototype (`VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1`, exercising the fused kernel):
- Baseline accuracy: 82.87%. Prototype: 82.94%. Δ +0.08pp (~1 question of 1319). Invalid rate 0.0% both arms.

## Performance

ABBA methodology (order A→C1→C1→A, isolated caches, no profiler, SHA-256 hash of output tokens to confirm determinism) on 5 workloads (decode B1/B8/B32, long-context B1, mixed B8), RTX 4090:

| Workload | Wall reduction | Throughput gain | Peak mem reduction |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| decode_b1 | +54.6% | +120.3% | 157.1 MiB |
| decode_b8 | +55.6% | +125.3% | 144.0 MiB |
| decode_b32 | +51.3% | +105.5% | 111.5 MiB |
| long_b1 | +31.2% | +45.3% | 111.5 MiB |
| mixed_b8 | +34.7% | +53.1% | 110.8 MiB |

All output-token hashes matched across all 4 processes/both arms for every workload (confirms determinism, not just aggregate timing).

## Known limitations

- The fused kernel is not yet in vLLM's JIT kernel-warmup path, so the first live inference call compiles it inline (observed latency spike). Warmup registration is out of scope for this PR.
- An unrelated, pre-existing lm_head `OutOfResources` (shared memory) bug in vLLM's own `linear_batch_invariant` persistent-matmul kernel was reproduced via one lightweight test harness at this vocab size; not related to this patch, not yet filed upstream, root cause not confirmed.

This PR was developed with Claude Code (Anthropic) assistance: kernel implementation, bug review, test authoring, and verification script development. All changed lines were reviewed by the human submitter (@ShengleiFu), who ran the test commands above and is able to defend this change end-to-end.

+    (chosen from which side of the M<=128 threshold a call falls on).
+    """
+
+    @dataclass(frozen=True)
+    class CompileKey:
+        N: int
+        K: int
+        GROUP_SIZE: int
+        BLOCK_SIZE_M: int
+        BLOCK_SIZE_N: int
+        BLOCK_SIZE_K: int = 32
+        NUM_STAGES: int = 2
+
+    kernel: ClassVar[Any] = staticmethod(awq_gemm_fused_fp32_kernel)
+
+    def dispatch(  # type: ignore[override]
+        self, *, m: int, N: int, K: int, GROUP_SIZE: int
+    ) -> CompileKey:
+        # The warmup tracer only supports a single expression-shaped body
+        # (conditional expressions, no if-statements/tuple-unpacking), so
+        # the tuned-vs-fallback choice is expressed with ternaries.
+        tuned_raw = _TUNED_TILES.get((N, K))
+        use_tuned = tuned_raw is not None
+        tuned = tuned_raw if tuned_raw is not None else (0, 0, 0, 0)
+        block_m = tuned[0] if use_tuned else (32 if m <= 128 else 128)
+        block_n = tuned[1] if use_tuned else (32 if m <= 128 else 64)
+        block_k = tuned[2] if use_tuned else 32
+        num_stages = tuned[3] if use_tuned else 2
+        return self.CompileKey(
+            N=N,
+            K=K,
+            GROUP_SIZE=GROUP_SIZE,
+            BLOCK_SIZE_M=block_m,
+            BLOCK_SIZE_N=block_n,
+            BLOCK_SIZE_K=block_k,
+            NUM_STAGES=num_stages,
+        )
+
+    def get_warmup_keys(
+        self, *, N: int, K: int, GROUP_SIZE: int = 128
+    ) -> list[CompileKey]:
+        # One representative M on each side of the 128 threshold covers both
+        # BLOCK_SIZE_M/N configs the SM89 fallback in dispatch(...) can
+        # select; for tuned shapes both traced M values collapse to
+        # the same (M-independent) CompileKey, so this over-covers safely.
+        return self._trace_dispatch(self.dispatch)(
+            m=(1, 129), N=N, K=K, GROUP_SIZE=GROUP_SIZE
+        )
+
+    def warmup_inputs(self, compile_key: CompileKey) -> dict[str, Any]:
+        # M is do_not_specialize'd, but __call__ re-dispatches from the input
+        # shape; one past BLOCK_SIZE_M lands on the same side of the SM89
+        # fallback's M <= 128 threshold as the key being warmed.
+        m = compile_key.BLOCK_SIZE_M + 1
+        num_groups = compile_key.K // compile_key.GROUP_SIZE
+        return dict(
+            input=TritonWarmupTensor(torch.float16, shape=(m, compile_key.K)),
+            qweight=TritonWarmupTensor(
+                torch.int32, shape=(compile_key.K, compile_key.N // 8)
+            ),
+            scales=TritonWarmupTensor(torch.float16, shape=(num_groups, compile_key.N)),
+            zeros=TritonWarmupTensor(
+                torch.int32, shape=(num_groups, compile_key.N // 8)
+            ),
+        )
+
+    @kernel_launcher
+    def __call__(
+        self,
+        input: torch.Tensor,
+        qweight: torch.Tensor,
+        scales: torch.Tensor,
+        zeros: torch.Tensor,
+    ) -> LaunchSpec:
+        m, k = input.shape
+        n = qweight.shape[1] * 8
+        group_size = k // scales.shape[0]
+        compile_key = self.dispatch(m=m, N=n, K=k, GROUP_SIZE=group_size)
+        output = (
+            TritonWarmupTensor(input.dtype, shape=(m, n))
+            if self._warming
+            else torch.empty((m, n), device=input.device, dtype=input.dtype)
+        )
+        grid = (
+            triton.cdiv(m, compile_key.BLOCK_SIZE_M)
+            * triton.cdiv(n, compile_key.BLOCK_SIZE_N),
+        )
+        return (
+            grid,
+            dict(
+                output_ptr=output,
+                M=m,
+                N=compile_key.N,
+                K=compile_key.K,
+                GROUP_SIZE=compile_key.GROUP_SIZE,
+                BLOCK_SIZE_M=compile_key.BLOCK_SIZE_M,
+                BLOCK_SIZE_N=compile_key.BLOCK_SIZE_N,
+                BLOCK_SIZE_K=compile_key.BLOCK_SIZE_K,
+                num_warps=4,
+                num_stages=compile_key.NUM_STAGES,
+            ),
+            output,
+        )
+
+
+_AWQ_GEMM_FUSED_FP32_KERNEL = AwqGemmFusedFp32Kernel()
+
+
+def register_awq_fused_fp32_warmup(*, N: int, K: int, GROUP_SIZE: int = 128) -> None:
+    _AWQ_GEMM_FUSED_FP32_KERNEL.register_warmup(N=N, K=K, GROUP_SIZE=GROUP_SIZE)
+
+
+def _awq_gemm_fused_fp32_impl(
+    inputs: torch.Tensor,
+    qweight: torch.Tensor,
+    scales: torch.Tensor,
+    qzeros: torch.Tensor,
+) -> torch.Tensor:
+    m, k = inputs.shape
+    n = qweight.shape[1] * 8
+    num_groups = scales.shape[0]
+    if inputs.dtype != torch.float16 or scales.dtype != torch.float16:
+        raise ValueError("fused AWQ GEMM supports FP16 inputs and scales only")
+    if qweight.dtype != torch.int32 or qzeros.dtype != torch.int32:
+        raise ValueError("fused AWQ GEMM requires int32 packed weights and zeros")
+    if not all(tensor.is_contiguous() for tensor in (inputs, qweight, scales, qzeros)):
+        raise ValueError("fused AWQ GEMM requires contiguous tensors")
+    if qweight.shape[0] != k:
+        raise ValueError("fused AWQ GEMM weight K does not match the input")
+    if num_groups == 0 or k % num_groups != 0:
+        raise ValueError(
+            "fused AWQ GEMM requires K to be an exact multiple of the number "
+            "of quantization groups"
+        )
+    group_size = k // num_groups
+    if group_size != 128:
+        raise ValueError("fused AWQ GEMM supports group_size=128 only")
+    if scales.shape != (num_groups, n):
+        raise ValueError("fused AWQ GEMM scales have an invalid shape")
+    if qzeros.shape != (num_groups, n // 8):
+        raise ValueError("fused AWQ GEMM zeros have an invalid shape")
+    if k % 32 != 0 or n % 32 != 0:
+        raise ValueError("fused AWQ GEMM requires K and N aligned to 32")
+
+    return _AWQ_GEMM_FUSED_FP32_KERNEL(inputs, qweight, scales, qzeros)
+
+
+def _awq_gemm_fused_fp32_fake(
+    inputs: torch.Tensor,
+    qweight: torch.Tensor,
+    scales: torch.Tensor,
+    qzeros: torch.Tensor,
+) -> torch.Tensor:
+    del scales, qzeros
+    return torch.empty(
+        (inputs.size(0), qweight.size(1) * 8),
+        dtype=inputs.dtype,
+        device=inputs.device,
+    )
+
+
+direct_register_custom_op(
+    op_name="awq_gemm_fused_fp32",
+    op_func=_awq_gemm_fused_fp32_impl,
+    mutates_args=[],
+    fake_impl=_awq_gemm_fused_fp32_fake,
+    dispatch_key=current_platform.dispatch_key,
+)
+
+
+def awq_gemm_fused_fp32(
+    inputs: torch.Tensor,
+    qweight: torch.Tensor,
+    scales: torch.Tensor,
+    qzeros: torch.Tensor,
+) -> torch.Tensor:
+    return torch.ops.vllm.awq_gemm_fused_fp32(inputs, qweight, scales, qzeros)

Thank you @yewentao256  for the feedback! Addressed both:

## 1. Diff size

Shrunk from ~566 to ~420 lines, kept only the regression tests tied to a specific bug fixed in this PR (group-count OOB validation, contiguity-independent dispatch) plus core shape-correctness and batch-invariance coverage. 

## 2. `lm_eval` — end-to-end accuracy

GSM8K, 5-shot, n=1319, same checkpoint (`Qwen/Qwen3-4B-AWQ`) and decoding config for both arms:

| Arm | strict-match | flexible-extract |
|---|---:|---:|
| Baseline (`VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=0`) | 83.78% ± 1.02 | 81.43% ± 1.07 |
| This PR (`VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1`, fused kernel) | 83.62% ± 1.02 | 81.20% ± 1.08 |

Both deltas are within stderr — no accuracy regression.

```
lm-eval run --model vllm \
  --model_args pretrained=Qwen/Qwen3-4B-AWQ,dtype=float16,quantization=auto_awq,max_model_len=2048,gpu_memory_utilization=0.85,trust_remote_code=True \
  --tasks gsm8k --batch_size auto
```

## 3. `vllm bench serve` — end-to-end perf

Both arms run with `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1` (the fused kernel only activates under batch-invariant mode, so a `BI=0` vs `BI=1` comparison would conflate "cost of batch-invariant mode itself" with "this kernel's effect," which isn't what this PR claims). Isolated legacy-dequant+matmul vs. the fused kernel via a `sitecustomize.py` monkeypatch of `awq_gemm_fused_fp32`, loaded into both the API server and its spawned engine-core worker via `PYTHONPATH` — real multiprocess `vllm serve`, not an in-process shortcut.

```
vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-4B-AWQ --quantization auto_awq --dtype float16 --max-model-len 2048 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.85 --trust-remote-code

vllm bench serve --backend vllm --model Qwen/Qwen3-4B-AWQ --dataset-name random \
  --random-input-len 512 --random-output-len 128 --num-prompts 200 --seed 0
```

Steady-state (2nd/3rd pass against an already-running server; see "Known limitations" for why the first pass is excluded):

| Arm | Mean TPOT | Output tok/s |
|---|---:|---:|
| Legacy (dequant+matmul) | ~59.7ms | ~3118 |
| This PR (fused kernel) | ~49.3ms | ~3180 |

~17% lower per-token decode latency, comparable-or-slightly-higher throughput.

**Known limitation surfaced by this run**: the fused kernel isn't yet in vLLM's JIT kernel-warmup path, so the very first live request against a freshly started server compiles it inline (one-time latency spike, logged as `Triton kernel JIT compilation during inference: awq_gemm_fused_fp32_kernel`). The table above reflects steady-state after that one-time cost; a production deployment would want warmup registration added (tracked as follow-up, not blocking this PR's correctness/perf claim).

Thanks @yewentao256 — I measured both. Short answer: it helps on Blackwell (SM120), not on Hopper, so the gate is now an exact per-arch, per-(N, K) allow-list rather than a `>= 90` threshold, and Hopper stays on the legacy path.

**Blackwell — RTX PRO 6000 (SM120): yes, for 2 of 4 shapes**
- Tile sweep (4 shapes × 12 tiles, one fixed tile per shape across M, all numerically correct and byte-identical across M; CUDA-event timing with L2 flush vs BI legacy): qkv_proj / gate_up_proj win with `(128,128,32,3)` — 1.4–1.5x / 2.7–3.2x at M ≤ 256, 0.90x / 0.88x at M = 4096. o_proj / down_proj had no tile that wins at small M without ~2x loss at M = 4096, so they stay legacy.
- `vllm bench serve`, `Qwen3-4B-AWQ`, BI on in both arms (same code, only the gate differs; OLD→NEW→NEW→OLD, fresh server each, default compile + CUDA graphs, 0 failed requests):

| scenario (in/out, rate) | output tok/s | mean TPOT | TTFT |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1024/128, 8 req/s | +3.9% | −30.5% | mean −11.1% |
| 128/1024, 8 req/s | +21.4% | −28.9% | mean −15.7% |
| 4096/32, 2 req/s | +0.4% | −25.3% | mean −1.8%, p99 +6.9% |
| 1024/256, rate=inf, 500 prompts | +5.3% | −5.8% | mean +7.0%, p99 +7.6% |

  Run-to-run spread ≤ 1.1% for tok/s and TPOT. The TTFT cost under backlog / long prompts is real (large-M prefill; matches the 0.88–0.90x at M = 4096).
- `lm_eval` gsm8k, full 1319, 5-shot: strict 0.8378 → 0.8362, flexible 0.8135 → 0.8135 (per-question flips 4/2 and 4/4).
- BI suite with `VLLM_TEST_MODEL=Qwen3-4B-AWQ`: 22/22 passed. Cold start with empty caches: warmup compiles exactly the key dispatch picks for M ∈ [1, 16384]; no JIT of this kernel after startup.

**Hopper — H800 PCIe (SM90): no**
- Under CUDA graph replay (8 distinct weight sets per graph, the serving execution mode), the Hopper tiles are 0.17–0.81x of BI legacy for every shape at every M; the same result with L2-flushed event timing.
